name: i18n house rules: English gettext sources and escape
query: This plugin is for Iranian sites. Admin notices and settings labels are currently written in Persian inside esc_html_e() and some buttons use bare _e() without escaping. Fix localization to match our house rules.
expected_behavior: Step 1: Route via wordpress-router; apply wp-dev-standards for i18n/string rules
Step 2: Enforce English-only source strings inside all gettext functions (__(), _e(), esc_html_e(), etc.)
Step 3: Replace Persian (or other non-English) literals inside gettext with clear English sources
Step 4: Do not 'fix' locale by hardcoding target language in PHP; use translation catalogs for fa_IR if needed
Step 5: Prefer esc_html_e / esc_html__ for HTML body text and esc_attr_e / esc_attr__ for attributes; avoid bare _e() for HTML
Step 6: Ensure text domain is a string literal matching the plugin slug (dashes, lowercase)
Step 7: Use sprintf/printf placeholders for dynamic values with translators: comments; no variable interpolation inside gettext templates
Step 8: Keep WP_Error codes as untranslated literals; translate only messages with English sources
Step 9: Run the localization checklist from wp-dev-standards before finishing
success_criteria: No non-English literals remain inside gettext/wp.i18n calls
User-visible HTML uses escaped i18n helpers where appropriate
Text domain is literal and matches plugin slug
Dynamic strings use placeholders, not concatenation or interpolated variables inside gettext
Error codes are not passed through __()
Target language (e.g. Persian) would come from .po/language packs, not from PHP source strings
